title: Why Games Feel So Hard to Stop
coreMove: Identify the stroke supply and life-position confirmation a game provides before asking someone to give it up.
sourcePressure: Unpacks strokes, time structuring, life positions, and the reason games persist even when they hurt.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Assuming a painful pattern continues because someone likes pain or lacks willpower, rather than because it reliably supplies recognition, structure, avoidance, or position proof.

sourceAnchors.name: stroke
sourceAnchors.detail: the source defines a stroke as a unit of social recognition and emphasizes that negative strokes are often preferred to no strokes
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A fight can feed a person in the thin way a negative stroke feeds: badly, but on time.

sourceAnchors.name: four life positions
sourceAnchors.detail: the source lists I'm OK, you're OK; I'm OK, you're not OK; I'm not OK, you're OK; and I'm not OK, you're not OK as positions games can confirm
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The game does not only create a bad feeling; it proves the old position again.

exampleSpecs.domain: night-shift warehouse complaint ritual before loading doors open
exampleSpecs.audience: a team lead who wants to stop the daily boss-bashing without removing the only reliable contact workers get
exampleSpecs.stakes: morale, safety checks, and a fragile sense of belonging
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Heather replaces the complaint circle with a two-minute load-risk check that still gives each person a turn and a nod.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Forklift backup beeps echo before the loading doors rise.

exampleSpecs.domain: freelance invoice chase with a late-paying client
exampleSpecs.audience: a designer who keeps entering a drama that proves clients never respect him
exampleSpecs.stakes: cash flow and a familiar grievance both arrive through the same pattern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas sets an automatic deposit rule before the next project instead of sending the fourth angry message that would supply proof.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 7:18 p.m., Nicolas refreshes the unpaid invoice for the sixth time.

exampleSpecs.domain: post-divorce co-parenting pickup at a swimming pool lobby
exampleSpecs.audience: a parent whose small accusations reliably pull the other parent into contact
exampleSpecs.stakes: the child's transition and both adults' stroke hunger are at stake
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Megan answers the pickup time and backpack contents only, then gets social contact elsewhere before the next handoff.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Chlorine hangs in the lobby while the child ties one wet shoelace.

exampleSpecs.domain: graduate seminar where one student always demolishes drafts
exampleSpecs.audience: a student using critique to confirm he is the only serious thinker in the room
exampleSpecs.stakes: peer trust and his own protection from inadequacy
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivier requires each critique to include one testable revision question, removing the superiority payoff while preserving recognition.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I just think the argument is naive," Olivier says, before anyone has opened their notebook.

exampleSpecs.domain: family small business rota where one sibling always arrives late
exampleSpecs.audience: a sibling who keeps proving she is the irresponsible one everyone expects
exampleSpecs.stakes: the shop opens short-staffed and the family story stays intact
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sofia sees that scolding supplies the role, so she changes the rota consequence and adds one clean place to earn trust.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Sofia four Saturdays to notice that the lecture was part of the schedule.

exampleSpecs.domain: online language-learning group that rewards self-deprecation
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who gets attention by announcing failure before trying
exampleSpecs.stakes: practice time is being traded for comforting strokes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Min posts one specific pronunciation clip and asks for one correction, replacing pity strokes with usable contact.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can get ten kind replies by saying you are hopeless before you record a single sentence.
